angle: Bottom up. I listed the 88 items of the 24 dynamics (59 exits, 23 transitions, 6 compose entries; read from /Users/ren/theories/theories/becoming/results/atlas/entries/dynamics.json, with the Lean statements checked for turned_by_loss, window_never_read, closed_stays_closed, outside_needed, outside_returns, kept_once_favoured, survivorsPersist_of_settled), wrote down every destination sentence, every 'between' pair and every law-of-staying sentence, and clustered the ones that say the same condition in different theorem wording. The clusters that recur became places; names came last. The largest clusters: 'locked / neither share nor rule falls / absorbed' (about 14 sentences), 'locked the other way / turned for good' (about 14), 'favours exactly where what comes back covers the cost' (10), 'not locked there / removal registered / tells apart again / couples apart' (18), 'kept for good although read / too late / past return' (8), 'no reader present, none readmitted / all hold it at every later step / fixed and closed under revision / registers no removal' (9), 'selected alike / unread' (many). AI-written.

coverage: Items in scope: 88 (59 exits, 23 transitions, 6 compose entries) over 24 dynamics; 5 of the 24 have no item (target-capture, a-reading-against-the-share-does-not-ratchet, capture-reaching-the-routes-of-correction, selection-for-narrowing-what-couples-in, self-reproducing-selection-across-carriers) and appear only as held_by. Arrows: 65 (41 exits, 21 transitions, 3 compose), of which 16 run both ways. Items counted as laws of staying (held_by, marked in the 'under' text): 5 (readings-revised exits 1, 3, 6; shaping-read transition 3; unselected exit 11). Unresolved: 18 (12 lead out of the region, 4 are identities that license shared places, 2 are witnesses that a premise binds or that show both sides of a threshold already drawn). 65 + 5 + 18 = 88. Arrows by strength as the data gives it: exact 23, sufficient 16, necessary 2, witness 14, reading 6, argued 2, stated 1, open 1. Four arrows repeat a law already cited by another dynamic (the two readings habit-lock and a-counter-rule cite the laws of capture-by-counted-choices, capture-through-the-rule and closed-capture), so 65 arrows rest on 61 distinct citations. Arrows by pair: held to/from held-other-side 11; pays-doers to/from costs-doers 10; outside-the-count to noticers-leaving 6; held-loss-growing to loss-registers 5; unsettled to one-view-left 4; one-view-left to loss-registers 4; noticers-leaving to loss-registers 4; noticers-leaving to too-late 4; outside-the-count to loss-registers 4; noticers-leaving to held-other-side 3; unsettled to held 2; noticers-leaving to one-view-left 2; outside-the-count to too-late 2; held to unsettled 1; held-loss-growing to noticers-leaving 1; loss-registers to/from too-late 1; noticers-leaving to pays-doers 1 (open).
what_the_layer_shows:
WHERE THE PLACES CONNECT. (a) The rule strand is solid: unsettled -> held by two pace bounds, and held <-> held-other-side by 11 items, five of them exact tipping counts. A person sees at once that a hold has a twin and that what separates them is a count. (b) The loss strand has one busy junction, 'those who'd notice are dwindling': seven neighbours, and four different ways on, each with a law: they object in time (held the other way, exact), they object too late (exact), they are gone before objecting (sufficient), the judging is taken out of the process's hands (sufficient). This junction is the real centre of the region, and the atlas has no node for it. (c) 'The loss now registers inside' collects 18 arrows from five places: every way out the region states ends there.

WHERE THEY DO NOT (holes worth drawing as holes).
1. Nothing leads INTO the closed form (held-loss-growing, the atlas's 元吸引子). Five arrows leave it; none arrives. What turns a plain hold into a hold with a growing uncounted loss is two premises (nothing outside is taken in; the loss grows each round), stated of no process. The likeness to family B's drain is said in prose and joined by no item.
2. Nothing leads on from 'the loss now registers' except to 'too late'. Which way a registered loss moves the rule is said only inside the rule-loop models, where the arrow skips this place and goes straight from dwindling noticers to the other hold. The two items that say 'registering is not yet restraint' (unselected exits 9, 10) point out of the region.
3. All six arrows from 'outside what it counts' to 'those who'd notice are dwindling' are readings, argued steps or one witness. The join between what a rule cannot count (family B) and who would tell it (family C) has no law. This is the loop chapter 02 section 10 reads as the meta-attractor's shape.
4. The pays/costs pair is internally the best proved part (10 items, 9 exact) and is tied to the rest by one open arrow only. Yet the laws that tie it exist: Becoming.RuleShaping.covering_locks and Becoming.DrawnShaping.drawn_rises with drawn_locks say that where changing the rule pays and the return rises with the changers' numbers, the hold forms. They sit in mechanisms and in my held_by, and no exit, transition or compose records them. The atlas could add this arrow from what is already proved.
5. 'One kind favoured, gaining' has no arrow at all. How a rule comes to be rebuilt from its winners is a premise everywhere (the records say so); the first link of the chain is a gap.
6. Nothing returns to 'not yet settled' except one arrow from the word-agreement dynamics. In the rule-loop models a hold is left only for the other hold or for 'registers'; there is no un-settling.
7. Chance appears in one dynamic only (shaping-read exit 2, transition 3); which holds noise leaves is a reading.
8. The two marked places (the checkers inside the loop; the pattern outliving its members) are islands: no item touches them. They are also what the project most wants to keep humans and AI out of. Drawn truthfully, the corner where rule-changing that pays meets the removal of noticers holds one open arrow, one reading and one open question.

WHAT ELSE IT SHOWS. The two word-agreement dynamics, which touch nothing in the atlas, land on three places of the chain without strain (unsettled, held, no other view left), and their exits say what the rule-loop's exits say: a dropped distinction comes back only from outside or by coining. So the layer joins by condition what the atlas could not join by law. Twelve of the 18 unresolved items point to places just over the border: ended (4), made good (2), each pushes by its own count (2), takes only what is spare, enough, fixed only on the cases met, below a regime's point (1 each). They show which neighbouring places to make next; 'ended' first. The optimum dynamic contributes laws of staying only: all four of its items lead out of the region.

DOES A PLACE RECUR IN OTHER FAMILIES. Yes for most. unsettled (F: cycles; any symmetric start); held and no-other-view-left (D: a view kept by its own update; G: closure; A: fixation); too-late (A: a regime's point); outside-the-count (all of B); pays/costs (all of E, and A's sorting among groups); loss-registers (B's ways out, D's pools). Proper to this region: held-loss-growing, noticers-leaving, and the two islands. So about nine of the fourteen would be shared, and a full layer of 30 to 40 looks reachable.
layout:
No axis carries a value. Left-right and up-down only keep joined places near each other; twins sit side by side at the same height so neither reads as above the other. Coordinates on a 12 by 9 grid (x to the right, y down).

Upper band, the rule and what it picks: favoured-gaining (0.3, 3), unsettled (2, 3), then the twin held (4.5, 3) | held-other-side (6.5, 3) drawn as one box split by a line labelled 'tipping count'; the eleven items between them are that line, not eleven arrows. To the right, a second twin: pays-doers (9, 4) | costs-doers (11, 4), likewise one split box for its ten items.

Lower band, what the rule does not count and who would notice, running right to left: outside-the-count (11.5, 7), noticers-leaving (6.5, 7) directly under held-other-side, so its 'objected in time' arrow goes straight up. held-loss-growing (3.5, 5) hangs under held, to its lower left. At the left edge: loss-registers (0.5, 6.5) with too-late (0.5, 8.5) under it, joined by a short two-way line. one-view-left (3.3, 6.1) sits inside the triangle held-loss-growing / noticers-leaving / loss-registers, so its arrows in and out stay inside that triangle.

Routes: outside-the-count -> noticers-leaving runs along y = 7; outside-the-count -> too-late and -> loss-registers run along the bottom edge, the second passing outside too-late. noticers-leaving -> pays-doers (open, dashed) goes up and right into empty space.

Islands, dashed outlines, no arrows: checks-inside (9.5, 6), placed between noticers-leaving and pays-doers because it is the two met one level up; outlives-members (11, 1.5).

Holes drawn as holes: a blank gap with a small label 'premise, not shown' between favoured-gaining and unsettled; an empty arrowhead socket on held-loss-growing facing held ('nothing leads in'); a faint stub from the pays/costs twin toward the held twin ('law proved, not entered as an arrow'); blank paper between loss-registers and unsettled ('which way it then moves: not said').

Line style carries how far seen: solid for exact, sufficient and necessary (a tick on necessary), dotted with a small w for witness, dashed for reading, argued and stated, dashed with an open head for open.

Crossings: one. The bundle unsettled -> one-view-left (four arrows from the word-agreement dynamics, drawn as one line) crosses held-loss-growing -> loss-registers, because one-view-left must sit inside the triangle. If that is unwanted, the word-agreement arrows can go in a small inset repeating the three places they use.
doubts:
Least sure, and choices I would argue against myself:

1. held and held-other-side as two places. They are one condition seen from two sides, and the theorem says so ('the lock belongs to how the rule reads, not the share it favours'). I split them because 'locked the other way' is the most frequent destination sentence in the data and the exits the project cares about end there. The cost: every tipping-count transition becomes a two-way arrow that the law itself says the loop never travels ('two regions the course never leaves'). I followed the instruction for 'exactly where' thresholds; a reader could take those arrows for movement. The split-box drawing is my answer; one place with a 'sides swap' loop is the alternative.

2. Window transitions as one-way forks. Where the data says 'for good' on both sides (loss-read transition 1, readers-drawn transition 2, lock-draws transition 1) I did not draw the two outcomes as a two-way pair; I drew one arrow from noticers-leaving for the branch the cited law states and left the other branch to the exit that states it. This departs from the letter of the both-ways rule.

3. The word-agreement dynamics on the chain's places. Their laws have no rule rebuilt from winners' numbers; I placed them by the shape of their sentences. Sending exits 3 to 5 to loss-registers (a merged distinction told apart again) and not back to unsettled is the weakest of these: after exit 5 everyone still holds one code.

4. pays-doers / costs-doers named generally. Bottom up, the cluster is 'what comes back to the doers against its cost' (Hamilton's rule), so the label lost 'control over the rule', which is the word the direction turns on. A top-down proposer would name it 'changing the rule pays'; I think the map should carry that as the capture chain's alias for this place.

5. too-late merges two senses (too few to tip the rule; the lost thing unrecoverable) that the atlas joins only as a reading with order not checked. Each half is a law; the merge is not. I gave how_far by the halves.

6. loss-registers is broad (four ways of registering) and is where 18 arrows end. It may be two places: 'seen by someone it counts' and 'the rule gives way'. I merged to stay within fourteen.

7. outside-the-count merges the blindness and the drain, and 'ended' is left over the border. The result is that the one dynamic added to the scope has all four items unresolved. For a layer of family B I would split these and add 'ended'.

8. The from-place of several arrows is my reading of the model, not a sentence in the item: noticers-leaving for the ReadInTime and Thinned laws (there the others 'dwindle' only in that the winners' part grows each round), and the open arrow noticers-leaving -> pays-doers for survivors exit 2, whose text says only that a join is not made.

9. favoured-gaining has no item and could be cut to make thirteen. I kept it because the gap after it is the first hole a reader should see.

10. 'Loss' in two labels. The record says the uncounted quantity is 'a count the loop does not read' and that calling it a loss is for a further reading. I kept the entries' own word because 'uncounted quantity' is not everyday speech.

11. Strength words: I kept the data's 'argued' and 'stated' beside 'reading' and 'open' and did not fold them. For transitions that are bounds or one-sided laws (pace bounds, the deadline, shaping-the-rule transition 3) I wrote 'sufficient'; the data gives transitions no strength field.

12. Chinese labels are mine, written by ear and not from the English, but they need a native speaker's ear before use; 查错的也在圈里 and 人换了，套路还在 are the two I am least sure of. Glosses and examples are English only. Examples are illustrations; none claims that an actual system meets a premise.

Read-only: nothing in the repository was changed; one scratch dump was written outside it at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ren-theories/d9ccfc76-7843-4b3c-ba5b-c950965917c6/scratchpad/scope.txt. No tests, builds or renders were run.
